requirements.title: Cryptographic inventory
requirements.text: The organization knows where and how public-key cryptography is used across its systems, products, and suppliers.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Inventory of cryptographic use
requirements.text: A maintained inventory records, for each system: the algorithms, key sizes or parameter sets, protocols, cryptographic libraries or modules, certificates, and the owning team.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Inventory covers products and embedded systems
requirements.text: The inventory includes cryptography inside purchased products, cloud services, embedded devices, and operational technology, not only in-house software.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.section: Prepare a cryptographic inventory; engage with technology vendors
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Quantum-vulnerable algorithm identification
requirements.text: Uses of algorithms that a cryptographically relevant quantum computer could break are identified and recorded.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.section: Quantum-vulnerable digital signature and key-establishment algorithms
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Quantum-vulnerable public-key use identified
requirements.text: Every use of RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, finite-field DH, and ECDH for key establishment or digital signatures is identified, linked to the systems that depend on it, and recorded as quantum-vulnerable.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Symmetric and hash strength reviewed
requirements.text: Symmetric ciphers and hash functions are reviewed against the target security category; uses below the organization's chosen strength (for example AES-128 where AES-256 is required by policy) are recorded.

citation.source: NSA, Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (CNSA 2.0) advisory, September 2022
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; CNSA 2.0 specifies AES-256 and SHA-384 or SHA-512 for National Security Systems; commercial targets may differ

requirements.title: Data longevity and harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure
requirements.text: Data that must stay confidential beyond the expected arrival of quantum attacks is identified and prioritized.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Confidentiality lifetime recorded per data class
requirements.text: Each data class has a recorded confidentiality lifetime (years the data must stay secret), and data classes whose lifetime extends past the organization's quantum-risk horizon are flagged as exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later collection.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; the comparison of data lifetime plus migration time against a threat horizon is a Sentinel method (commonly attributed to Mosca), not a NIST requirement

requirements.title: Crypto agility
requirements.text: Systems can change cryptographic algorithms and parameters without major redesign.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Algorithms are configurable
requirements.text: Cryptographic algorithms and parameter sets are selected through configuration or a central library, so a change of algorithm does not require application code changes in each system.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Vendor and supplier roadmap
requirements.text: Suppliers' plans for supporting the NIST post-quantum standards are known and tracked.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Vendor PQC roadmaps obtained
requirements.text: For each critical product or service that uses public-key cryptography, the vendor's planned support for FIPS 203, 204, or 205 and the target date are obtained in writing and tracked.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Migration plan
requirements.text: A risk-prioritized plan moves systems from quantum-vulnerable algorithms to NIST post-quantum standards.

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Prioritized migration roadmap
requirements.text: A documented roadmap with named owners and target dates prioritizes systems by data longevity, exposure, and criticality, and its dates are checked against the IR 8547 transition timeline (and CNSA 2.0 where National Security Systems are in scope).

citation.source: CISA, NSA, and NIST, Quantum-Readiness: Migration to Post-Quantum Cryptography (fact sheet), August 2023
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Key establishment target uses ML-KEM
requirements.text: The target state for key establishment uses ML-KEM with a parameter set (ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, or ML-KEM-1024) chosen for the required security category.

citation.source: NIST FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM), August 13, 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; section number to be confirmed

requirements.title: Signature target uses ML-DSA or SLH-DSA
requirements.text: The target state for digital signatures uses ML-DSA (ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, or ML-DSA-87) or SLH-DSA, with the choice and parameter set recorded per use case (for example SLH-DSA for long-lived firmware signing roots).

citation.source: NIST FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA), August 13, 2024
citation.section: ML-DSA parameter sets; see also FIPS 205 SLH-DSA parameter sets
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; section numbers to be confirmed

requirements.title: Hybrid deployment
requirements.text: Where interoperability or assurance requires it, post-quantum and classical algorithms are combined during the transition.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Hybrid key establishment where used is documented
requirements.text: Where hybrid key establishment (a classical algorithm combined with ML-KEM) is deployed, the combination, the protocol, and the plan to retire the classical component are documented.

citation.source: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards, November 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; IR 8547 was an initial public draft in Nov 2024; check whether a final version exists and whether the 2030 deprecation and 2035 disallowance dates changed

requirements.title: Testing and validation
requirements.text: Post-quantum implementations are tested for interoperability and performance and come from validated modules.

citation.source: NIST FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM), August 13, 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it

requirements.title: Interoperability and performance tested
requirements.text: Before production, post-quantum implementations are tested for interoperability with peers and for the effect of larger keys, ciphertexts, and signatures on handshakes, storage, and constrained devices; results are recorded.

citation.source: NIST FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA), August 13, 2024
citation.section: Key and signature sizes by parameter set
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; Sentinel testing requirement; size figures are in the parameter set tables of FIPS 203, 204, and 205

requirements.title: Validated implementations used
requirements.text: Production implementations of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA are validated under the NIST Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program and come from FIPS 140-3 validated modules where the organization requires validated cryptography.

citation.source: NIST FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard (SLH-DSA), August 13, 2024
citation.note: Sentinel requirement derived from the cited source; not text from it; CAVP and CMVP program references to be confirmed

name: Post-Quantum Cryptography Readiness
sourceEdition: Sentinel model 1.0 based on FIPS 203, 204, 205 (August 13, 2024) and NIST IR 8547 ipd (November 2024)
publisher: Sentinel Assess (derived from NIST, CISA, and NSA publications)
description: A readiness model for migrating from quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography (RSA, elliptic curve, finite-field Diffie-Hellman) to the NIST post-quantum standards ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204), and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). The requirements are Sentinel requirements derived from the standards and government guidance; they are not quoted from them.
